groups.title: Soft Capsule (E12800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; signs of shock (rarely, urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; severe skin reactions with fever, erythema and many small pustules; asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like).

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E83400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins B1, B2, B6 and D in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), beriberi, eye fatigue, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; or if you have had kidney stones.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins B1, B2, B6, D and of zinc, relief of neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, beriberi, eye fatigue, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets

groups.caution:

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (D57400APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, a feeling of a blocked stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid eructation (sour belching), loss of appetite, indigestion, overeating and promotion of digestion.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 1.6 g per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 1.1 g per dose. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: 0.8 g per dose. Ages 5 years to under 8 years: 0.5 g per dose. Ages 3 years to under 5 years: 0.4 g per dose. Ages 1 year to under 3 years: 0.3 g per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, with an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are receiving dialysis, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, if you have high blood pressure, if you are an older person, if you have heart or kidney impairment or oedema, or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with a tetracycline antibiotic. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).

If constipation or diarrhoea occurs, or if the amount of urine decreases, the face, hands or feet swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises, or headache or myopathy (weakness, cramp or trembling of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Capsule (208204ACE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 20000 to 40000 EP units of lipolytic activity with each meal. Children aged 4 years to under 12 years: take 500 EP units of lipolytic activity per kg of body weight with each meal. Swallow the capsules whole during a meal or immediately after it with plenty of water. If the capsule cannot be swallowed whole, as in children or older people, open the capsule, mix the contents with liquid or soft food and swallow the contents immediately without chewing them. The duration of treatment depends on the severity of the disease. The dose always varies with the severity of the pancreatic damage and the composition of the meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it, if you have had hypersensitivity to beef or pork, if you have acute pancreatitis, or if you have an acute attack of chronic pancreatitis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have cystic fibrosis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have or have had gout, kidney failure or high blood uric acid; or if you have a hypersensitivity reaction to proteins of pig origin.

Do not chew this medicine or open the capsule to take it. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Any dose adjustment that is needed must be made under a doctor's supervision and follows the improvement of symptoms such as fatty stools or abdominal pain. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a folic acid preparation, acarbose or miglitol.

The fine powder of this medicine irritates the nasal mucosa and the airways, and inhaling it may cause asthma. Take care when taking it.

If skin allergy or hypersensitivity, skin rash, sneezing, watering of the eyes, an immediate allergic reaction such as bronchospasm, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal distension, abnormal bowel movements, fibrosing colonopathy, high uric acid in the urine, high uric acid in the blood, distal intestinal obstruction syndrome, asthma, urticaria, itching, or ulcers in the mouth or around the anus occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (A98500ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Toxicity may occur if a child aged 6 years or younger takes this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have Wilson's disease, haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gallbladder disease, gout or kidney stones; or if you are short of folic acid.

It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever or coma occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have gout; if you have or have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an intravenous lipid preparation.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea or loose stools occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
